basis.governing_question: Should Quinta Azul enter the Spanish retail market and, if so, how?

sub_questions.question: How large and attractive is the Spanish retail market for Quinta Azul's olive oil?
Who competes there, and what do Spanish retail buyers and shoppers need?
Does Quinta Azul have the assets and capabilities to win in Spain?
Which entry options exist for Spain, and does the business case support a go or no-go?
If the answer is go, what entry plan and roadmap should Quinta Azul follow?

work.unit: Market assessed in full (demand, channels, competitors, regulation, buyer interviews)

phase_work.why: Spain is assessed as one market in full; the capability check and leadership interviews run alongside it.

work.unit: Entry option and business case for one market
Entry sequence and roadmap across markets

phase_work.why: The entry option and business case for Spain come first, then the entry roadmap, one after the other.

sizing.levers: Assessing only the retail channels the CEO and Commercial Director prioritize, and starting the roadmap alongside the business case, would shorten the engagement most.

phases.name: Research
phases.objective_one_line: Assess the size, competition and buyer needs of the Spanish retail market and Quinta Azul's capability to win there.

gate.label: Findings sign-off
gate.decision: Is Spain attractive enough to justify designing entry options?

phases.name: Design
phases.objective_one_line: Compare entry options for Spain, build the business case and draft the entry roadmap for the go or no-go.

gate.label: Final readout
gate.decision: Approve the Spain go or no-go decision and, if go, the entry plan?

architect_notes: Engagement length is not given, so the 7 to 10 weeks are an estimate from the sizing; confirm length and any deadline before quoting.
Design is sized for a go outcome; a no-go would drop the entry roadmap and shorten the phase.
